turns.text: Is every delivery route paying for itself this quarter?

{"sql": "SELECT route, SUM(amount) AS total_route_cost, COUNT(*) AS n, MIN(effective_on) AS first_dt, MAX(effective_on) AS last_dt\nFROM ledger WHERE kind='route_cost' AND effective_on >= '2026-07-01' AND effective_on <= '2026-09-30'\nGROUP BY route"}
turns.name: run_sql

turns.text:
{"sql": "SELECT i.route, SUM(l.qty*(l.unit_price-l.unit_cost)) AS gross_margin, SUM(l.qty*l.unit_price) AS revenue, COUNT(DISTINCT i.invoice_no) AS n_invoices
FROM erp_invoices i JOIN erp_invoices_lines l ON l.parent_id = i.invoice_no
WHERE i.issued_on >= '2026-07-01' AND i.issued_on <= '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY i.route"}
turns.name: run_sql

## Delivery route profitability check

**Data limitation:** Today is 2026-09-29, but the system's invoice and route-cost ledger data stop at 2026-06-30 / 2026-04-01 respectively. There is no data yet for the current quarter (Q3 2026, Jul-Sep), so I can't answer for "this quarter" literally. I used the most recently completed quarter with full data, Q2 2026 (Apr 1 - Jun 30), where route costs are booked as a lump sum on 2026-04-01 (13 weeks × weekly_cost) and margin comes from invoice line items issued in that window.

**Q2 2026 results (gross margin vs. quarterly route cost):**

| Route | Name | Gross margin | Route cost | Net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | North loop | $38,030.99 | $5,200.00 | +$32,830.99 |
| R2 | City | $14,664.92 | $4,940.00 | +$9,724.92 |
| R3 | South loop | $4,200.02 | $6,500.00 | -$2,299.98 |

R1 and R2 comfortably cover their route cost. **R3 (South loop) did not pay for itself** in Q2 2026: its gross margin fell about $2,300 short of its $6,500 quarterly route cost.

This is exactly the kind of quarterly cost-vs-margin comparison the routes policy calls for, so R3 is a candidate for that review. I haven't taken any action (no order, hold, or message was requested, and there's no "route cost adjustment" action in the toolset) but wanted to flag it before you decide whether to renegotiate the route cost or investigate why margin is thin there.

ANSWER: Q3 2026 has no invoice or route-cost data in the system yet, so it can't be assessed; using the last complete quarter (Q2 2026), routes R1 and R2 covered their cost well but R3 (South loop) ran a shortfall of about $2,300 against its $6,500 quarterly cost.
